title: fix(sim): the field ceiling bounds a chord's travel, not a wide tool's footprint (#4079)
body:
## What changed

`SdfField::subtract_batch` (`field_cut.rs`) refused a chord when its swept window, clipped to the cut region, passed `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` (1 << 22). A wide tool's own footprint can pass that count. Then a short move was refused, and segmenting could not help. The column engine cuts the same move.

The ceiling now bounds the cells that the chord's travel adds: the cells of the clipped window minus the cells of the same solid at rest at the chord's start, with the same reach, padding and clipping.

- `Sweep::rest_window` (new, `field_sweep.rs`): the window of the solid with its path collapsed to its start. It lies inside `Sweep::window`. It is `None` for the lathe sweep, which keeps the old bound.
- `window_of` now calls `window_between(sw, p0, p1, ...)`. The window of a chord is unchanged.
- The refusal message names the new bound ("... cells beyond the tool at rest ...") and still asks the caller to segment the move.

A short move of any tool passes. A long chord still refuses, and segmenting always brings it under the ceiling.

Not changed: the f32 cut twin (`cut_twin_work.rs`, `TWIN_MAX_CELLS_PER_CHORD`) states the same value for its own work list. That is a follow-up if you want the two laws to stay the same.

## Readings

A 120 x 120 x 30 mm block at cell 0.254 mm, a flat tool 50.8 mm across, a feed at z 25:
- A 1 mm move: refused before; cuts now. The faced top is air, and stock stays below the face and outside the tool.
- A 120 mm chord: refused before and now.
- The same chord in 24 pieces of 5 mm: cuts.

## Pinning tests

`crates/sim/tests/field_wide_tool.rs`, synthetic shapes only, 2 tests:
- `a_wide_tools_short_move_cuts_on_the_field_engine_as_on_the_column_engine`: fails on the old code (refused on op 0).
- `a_wide_tools_long_chord_still_refuses_and_its_segments_cut`.

The existing pin `an_unpayable_window_refuses_and_writes_nothing` (`stock_sdf_cut.rs`) still refuses. `stock_sdf_cut`, `stock_field_cost`, `field_arc_sweep` and `stock_backend_parity` pass.

## Gates

On the final head `f9d231e63` (upstream/main merged in):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 85 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 27.6 min.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: green, 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 96.5 min (most of it the release build, on a shared box).
- No heavy step: this is not a `P1` (work-issue section 3).

The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/4079-wide-tool-ceiling.md`.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (they run at the cut).
- The GUI.

title: docs(research): HEIDENHAIN control dialects and the Picomax 55 review
body:
## What is in it

This PR adds research notes in `docs/research/heidenhain/`. The notes tell which words, cycles and cycle parameters each HEIDENHAIN TNC control accepts, and from which NC software version.

- `README.md`: the method, the coverage and the top findings.
- `dialects.md`: a proposal for `controller.identity` values, capability flags and profiles (control + NC software → flags).
- `differences.md`: the common language, the additions of each series, post-relevant features with "introduced / changed / removed", and the Q-parameter lists of cycles 200, 203, 205, 207 and 209.
- `differences-by-version.md`: the new-function entries of each NC software version (generated, short pointers only).
- `cycles.md`: 211 cycle numbers with the HEIDENHAIN name, a purpose, the DIN/ISO code, the option, the versions and a reference.
- `inventory.md`: each manual with its ID, title, edition date and download URL.
- `picomax-55-review.md`: the review of the two HEIDENHAIN posts and `fehlmann-picomax55.mch` against the Fehlmann manual and the machine parameters.

## Method

- The sources are the public HEIDENHAIN user manuals and the "Overview of New and Modified Software Functions" documents from the TNCguide portal.
- The text of each PDF was extracted with `pdftotext -layout`, and scripts searched the text.
- Each fact has a HEIDENHAIN document ID and a PDF page. A gap is marked "unsure" or "not found".
- The Q lists (B3) come from the example block that starts with the cycle's own number and name, up to the next NC block. Each row has the manual ID and the PDF page.
- Section C applies the "not TNC 410" marks of the shared ISO manual 345 940-22. A bullet that names a different software version than its heading is removed.
- Each profile in `dialects.md` has a source column. A cell without full evidence is "unknown".

## What is not in it

- No manual, no extracted manual text and no local path. The files hold facts with document references and short phrases only.
- No access codes, passwords or file names that identify the single machine. The review keeps the MP numbers and values.
- No code change.

## How it feeds the issues

- #4095: `dialects.md` is the proposal for the dialect selection.
- #4093 and #4094: the version thresholds for `FUNCTION DWELL` and for Q395/Q208 are in `differences.md` (B2, B3).
- #4085, #4086, #4087 and #4088: the review gives the evidence (MP values and manual pages).
- #3095: the review lists what to test on the real iTNC 530 340490-03.

## Review fix (head 5a1fddf15)

- B3 made again; the old rows that mixed in other cycles are gone.
- TNC 320 Q208/Q395 at 77185x-01 (was -05) in all copies.
- TNC 410 section of `differences-by-version.md` removed; TNC 410 rows in `cycles.md` and the TNC 410 profile corrected.
- TNC 426/430 profile split at 280 474 (cycle 205) and 280 476 (M140, cycle 247).
- Picomax review link in `dialects.md` fixed.

title: fix(wire): a work bottom at the lower guide is within reach
body:
## The report

The user (v0.26.0) put the origin at the part bottom and made a Wire Contour. The post was blocked:

```
post blocked - Wire Contour1: work bottom Z-0.000 is below the lower guide Z0.000, outside the guides' reach
```

## The cause

The guide-reach law (`check_guide_span` in `crates/app/src/operation/wire_verify.rs`) compared the work with each guide plane with a strict `<` / `>`. The work bottom is the lowest facet Z of the part or stock in world Z. The guide plane is the stated guide Z plus the WCS origin Z. The two values come from two different float paths: the origin is written from a box (the anchor buttons read the stock box or the part bounds, in the setup frame), and the facets are moved by their own transform. They can differ by round-off, for example 1e-12. The strict comparison read that round-off as a gap, and `{:.3}` printed it as "Z-0.000". The test reproduces the exact message with an origin at Z1e-12.

The same strict comparison was in two more places:

- `judge_pose` in `crates/app/src/machine/wire_edm.rs` (a tapered or 4-axis pose against the guides; message "rides Z-0.000 ...").
- the native Agie job check in `crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`.

The upper guide had the mirror bug ("work top Z12.000 is above the upper guide Z12.000").

## The fix

- `app::machine::wire_edm::GUIDE_REACH_TOL` = `wire_edm::PATH_TOL` (10 nm, the wire path's existing tolerance). No new number.
- `below_guide` / `above_guide` compare within that tolerance. A NaN height is refused. All three places use them. The span check runs for each wire post (generic ISO, Sodick, G-EDM) through `wire_verdict`; the Agie job check has its own call.
- `reach_z` / `guide_z` write the message heights. They never write "-0.000". When a refused height and its guide read the same in three decimals, six decimals are written, so that a refused gap never reads as no gap.
- A real gap is still refused by name.

Decision: `docs/decisions/4039-wire-guide-zero.md`.

## Readings

- Before the fix: origin Z1e-12, lower guide Z0 gives `work bottom Z-0.000 is below the lower guide Z0.000`. Origin Z-1e-12, upper guide Z12 gives `work top Z12.000 is above the upper guide Z12.000`.
- After the fix: these cases post. A 0.01 mm gap gives `work bottom Z-0.010 is below the lower guide Z0.000`. A 0.0001 mm gap gives `work bottom Z-0.000100 is below the lower guide Z0.000`. A 0.01 mm gap above the upper guide gives `work top Z12.010 is above the upper guide Z12.000`.

## Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/wire_taper.rs`)

- `a_work_bottom_at_the_lower_guide_is_within_reach`: a vertical and a 3 degree tapered punch post with the origin Z at 0, 1e-12 and 0.1 + 0.2 - 0.3; a 0.01 mm and a 0.0001 mm gap are refused by name (vertical), and a 0.01 mm gap is refused for the tapered cut.
- `a_work_top_at_the_upper_guide_is_within_reach`: the mirror at the upper guide.

Both failed on `origin/main` with the user's message, and pass with the fix. The existing guide tests in the same file (`work_below_the_lower_guide_blocks_the_post`, `work_above_the_upper_guide_blocks_the_post`, `guide_limits_use_the_setup_origin_and_include_stock_above_the_part`, `a_uv_offset_past_the_stroke_or_the_guides_is_refused_by_name`) keep their exact messages.

## Not exercised

- The user's own model and project: the round-off is reproduced through the WCS origin, not through the user's file.
- The Agie job check has no test of its guide refusal (none existed before). Its change is the same helper call.
- No real EDM control.

## Gate

All on head `2b38273d6` (log `4039-2b38273d6.log`, first line the head SHA), macOS:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 351 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. It includes `wire_taper`, `wire_verify`, `wire_post`, `wire_4axis` and the other wire suites, and the example catalog suites `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` (all ok).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- P3: no heavy step.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a part with its origin at the part bottom posts when the lower guide is at Z0; the guide-reach check no longer reads float round-off as a gap, and its messages never print "-0.000".

title: feat(tools): ISO 13399 tool components, ISO 1832 and ISO 5608 codes, fit checks
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the pure tool component model to `camcraft-tools`. It is the first issue of the component track (#3642, then #3643 to #3648). It adds no ECS code, no file I/O and no new crate edge.

- `component.rs`: `ToolComponent` with the three ISO 13399 kinds.
  - `CuttingItem`: an `InsertSpec`, or a solid `Tool` with its shank connection.
  - `ToolItem`: one machine side (MCS) and one or more insert seats (`CSW1`, `CSW1_2`, ...).
  - `AdaptiveItem`: one MCS and one CSW.
  - `ToolComponent::new` checks the component when it is made. The fields are private, so each component that exists is valid.
- `connection_code.rs`: `ConnectionCode`, one normalized type for ADINTMS and ADINTWS. It has steep tapers (BT, CAT, SK), HSK, PSC (ISO 26623), KM (ISO 26622), ER (ISO 15488), Weldon (DIN 1835-B), cylindrical shank, TTS, rectangular shank (ISO 5608), VDI, BMT, shell mill arbor and a custom name. Sizes must be in the published series.
- `insert_codes.rs` and `insert_iso1832.rs`: the ISO 1832 insert code, positions 1 to 7 (shape, clearance, tolerance, fixing, size, thickness, corner). The inscribed circle is derived from the shape.
- `insert_seat.rs`: `InsertSeatSpec` (clamping, shape, approach angle, clearance, hand, size, optional thickness) and the ISO 5608 holder code parser.
- `component_fit.rs`: `check_insert_fit`, `check_coupling_fit`, `compatible_parents` and `compatible_children`. Each refusal (`FitError`) gives both component names, the property, the expected value and the actual value.
- `docs/decisions/3642-tool-components.md` records the rules and what was dropped.

The rules are general machining practice. The code tables are the ones that tool vendors publish. No standard text is copied.

## Readings

- `CNMG120408` gives IC 12.7 mm, thickness 4.76 mm and nose radius 0.8 mm. `TCMT110204` gives IC 6.35 mm: the edge is 10.998 mm, and the size code is the edge cut to whole mm after 0.02 mm.
- `PCLNR2525M12` gives clamping P, approach angle 95 degrees, a 25 x 25 shank and a length of 150 mm.
- Example refusal text: `'SPKN1203EDL' does not fit 'CSSPR2525M12': hand - expected R, actual L`.

## Pinning tests (camcraft-tools lib)

- `insert_designation_tests::common_turning_inserts_parse`
- `insert_designation_tests::common_milling_inserts_parse`
- `insert_designation_tests::designations_round_trip_through_their_text`
- `insert_designation_tests::malformed_insert_codes_are_refused_by_position`
- `insert_designation_tests::turning_holder_codes_parse_and_round_trip`
- `insert_designation_tests::malformed_holder_codes_are_refused_by_position`
- `insert_designation_tests::connection_codes_round_trip_and_refuse_by_name`
- `insert_designation_tests::a_plain_bore_takes_a_weldon_shank_but_not_the_reverse`
- `insert_designation_tests::degenerate_codes_never_panic` (5000 pseudo-random texts, with empty, short and non-ASCII input)
- `component_fit_tests::inserts_fit_the_holders_made_for_them`
- `component_fit_tests::insert_mismatches_are_refused_by_name` (shape, clearance, size, thickness, clamping and fixing, hand, port, kind)
- `component_fit_tests::couplings_match_by_connection_code` (coupling code, Weldon flat)
- `component_fit_tests::the_library_queries_find_parents_and_children`
- `component_fit_tests::malformed_components_are_refused_by_name`

## Gate (Windows, winbuild)

All runs are on the final head `57f36190017c9f3dc547022285c1e96696ec376e`, on Windows (winbuild, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`).

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (log `gate-3642-57f361900.log`, first line is the head SHA): the plan is 1 step, `tools suites: lib`. Result: ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-tools --lib -- component insert_designation`: 14 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- P6: no heavy step. No post or toolpath changed, so no `example_catalog*` suite is needed.

## Not exercised

- No caller uses the model yet. The assembly resolver (#3643), the document table and commands (#3644), the stores and the project file (#3645), multi-seat cutters (#3646), MCP (#3647) and the UI (#3648) come later.
- No Mac or Linux build. The code is plain Rust with no platform code.

## Left for #3643 and later

- The components have no serde. #3645 owns the `camcraft-components/1` format.
- The ids are plain strings. #3644 and #3645 decide how ids are made and kept.
- The ISO 5608 parser reads rectangular-shank holders. A boring bar (ISO 6261) or a cutter body gets its seats as `InsertSeatSpec` values made directly.
- A seat has no frame (position or rotation). The frames are #3643.

No command is added, so no MCP tool is owed.

title: fix(multiaxis): start and exit picks for the 5-axis parallel
body:
## What changes

Slice 3 of #3330: the 5-Axis Parallel (`Parallel5D`) takes a start point and an exit point. The kind now has the existing `PickCapability::Raster` ("the corner of the first raster row and the end of the last row").

A zigzag raster of fixed passes can start at four corners only: each end of the first pass and of the last pass. Each corner is one order of the same passes:
- reverse the pass order, or not;
- run every pass the other way, or not.

The zigzag alternation stays in all four orders. The new module `finishing3d::raster_seam` selects the order before the raster's link step (`raster_pass_seamed`). Then `multiaxis::parallel5d_seamed` poses the path with the same stamp.

- **Start:** the corner nearest the pick.
- **Exit alone:** the order whose last pass ends nearest the pick.
- **Start and exit:** of the orders whose start is in reach of the start pick, the order whose end is in reach of the exit pick. The smallest sum of the two distances wins. At a tie, the automatic order wins.
- A pick with a Z is read in 3D, to the tool tip. A pick without a Z is read in XY.
- The geometry of each pass does not change. The raster's own laws (`march::emit_runs`) plan the links between passes on the new order. The tilt limit, the shank dodge and the centre-cut guard read the path after the re-order.
- Cut direction: the raster cuts both ways by its zigzag law and does not read `climb`. Parallel5D has no one-way mode. Thus no order asks for a direction that the operation forbids. The waterline rings after the raster keep their climb order.
- No pick: the passes stay as they are. The path is byte-identical.

The decision, with the dropped options, is in `docs/decisions/3330-parallel5d-picks.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never moved)

- A pick farther than 1.5 tool diameters from every corner of its role: `start point (x, y): the raster can start only at a corner (an end of its first or its last pass); the nearest corner (...) stands d mm away, farther than ...`. The exit pick has the same text.
- An exit that no order from the start pick can end at: `exit point (...): a raster that starts at the start point ends at (...) - farther than ... from the exit point; ...`.
- A pick on a raster with no pass (no shallow ground in the depths).
- A seam on a pattern other than the one-direction Parallel raster. Only Parallel5D reads a seam.

**Plunge and retract columns: there is no new refusal, on purpose.** Each corner is a raster sample. The raster keeps a sample only where the ball's vertical column up to the clearance plane is clear (`support::plunge_support`). With shank avoidance, the stamp checks the shank at each cut station with a column that is open upward (`avoid::shank_hits`). Thus the plunge station and the last cut station already prove the shank column. A new column check could not fire, and no mutation of it could turn a test red. The pins hold the law that the pick depends on instead (see M5 below).

## Mutation table

Each mutation was applied by itself to head `9af967e38`. Then `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test multiaxis raster_seam` ran on winbuild, and the change was reverted. M6 ran again on `b9101ecb1`, after a fix to the pin.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | The start reach check removed (`retain` with `f64::INFINITY`) | RED: `raster_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`, `raster_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_stay_clear_or_are_refused_by_name` |
| M2 | The exit consistency check removed (exit filtered only without a start) | RED: `raster_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M3 | Order ignored (always the automatic order) | RED: `raster_start_point_...`, `raster_exit_point_...`, `raster_picked_columns_...` |
| M4 | Flip dropped (pass order only) | RED: `raster_start_point_...`, `raster_exit_point_...` |
| M5 | The raster column trim disabled (`plunge_support` keeps samples under a canopy) | RED: `raster_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_stay_clear_or_are_refused_by_name` (the 0.25 mm ball sweep over the chosen corner hits the canopy) |
| M6 | An empty seam reverses the passes | RED: `raster_without_a_pick_is_the_automatic_path_byte_for_byte`, `raster_start_point_...` |

In the first M6 run, the byte-identity pin stayed green. Both sides of that pin go through the seamed code, so the pin compared the code with itself. The pin now also asserts the automatic start corner by itself: ball centre (40, 1, 3). M6 now turns it red.

## Readings

- The automatic raster on the 40 x 30 floor with a block starts at ball centre (40, 1, 3). Its first row runs toward -X: a rim row takes the parity of its neighbour.
- Canopy fixture: a plate that leans 50 degrees over the (0, 0) corner, z 10 to 20. A pick at (0, 0) is refused, because the nearest corner is farther than 9 mm. A pick at (6, 0) starts or ends at a corner with x > 6, and its column sweep is clear.

## Pinning tests

`camcraft-motion`, suite `multiaxis` (new module `multiaxis/raster_seam.rs`):
- `raster_without_a_pick_is_the_automatic_path_byte_for_byte`
- `raster_start_point_starts_the_cut_at_the_nearest_corner` (the far end of the first pass: each pass runs the other way; the automatic end: the whole raster runs back)
- `raster_exit_point_ends_the_last_pass_at_the_nearest_corner` (the last cut ends at the corner, and the tool rises straight up)
- `raster_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`
- `raster_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_stay_clear_or_are_refused_by_name`

Each picked path is sampled every 0.25 mm along each move:
- every move: the ball sinks no more than the tolerance into a facet (no gouge, no link through a wall);
- every raster cut lies on a cut of the automatic raster (the geometry does not change, and the count of cuts is the same).

`camcraft-app`, suite `start_exit_shared` (new module `start_exit_shared/parallel5d.rs`, and one arm in the capability test):
- `parallel5d_starts_at_the_picked_corner_and_ends_at_the_picked_exit` (through `operation::generate`; cuts sampled every 0.25 mm against the automatic raster; no pick gives the same path)
- `parallel5d_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name`
- `parallel5d_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` (MCP `edit_operation`, `undo`, `redo`; the `edit_operation` schema names the raster kind)
- `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (Parallel5D is `Raster`)

## Goldens

No golden moved. The example catalog suites ran in the quick gate (see below).

## Windows gate (winbuild)

Log `C:\camcraft-logs\gate-3330c-3835572b7c1f9cc1c3040279fc422af40b22b224.log`. Its first line is the head SHA `3835572b7`. This head is the branch after `git merge origin/main` (`034e91b8b`). The merge base is `034e91b8b`. The merge had one conflict, in the `s_edit_op` text of `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`: main added the sinker and hole-order words, and this PR added the raster clause. Both are kept.

| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=5`, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_STALL_MIN=45`) | 237 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (61.9 min). This includes the 36 motion suites (`multiaxis`, `finish3d*`, `pivot5d`, ...), `example_catalog` / `_adaptive` / `_edge_work`, `golden_cl`, `first_part_programs`, `mcp_doc_drift` and `start_exit_shared` |
| `cargo xtask gate light` | 6 steps, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Earlier attempts:
- Attempt 1 on `b9101ecb1`: the `app build (--no-run)` step stalled. The watchdog stopped it after 15 minutes with no output, while link.exe was still alive. Clippy found one `ptr_arg` error, fixed in `59a326e83`.
- Attempt 2 on `59a326e83`: all green (237 / 6 / clean). Then `main` moved and gave the conflict above.

The stall watchdog was set to 45 minutes for the next attempts, because winbuild needs more than 15 minutes to link the 237 app test binaries with 5 jobs.

No heavy step: this PR is P2 ("Heavy lanes at review").

## Not exercised

- No UI rows for the picks on the operation page. As in slices 1 and 2, the picks ride `edit_operation` and the viewport pick. The page no longer shows "not taken" for this kind.
- A tilted (3+2) setup frame: the picks are read in the generator's frame, as in slices 1 and 2.
- Shank avoidance in the motion pins. The column law for the shank is read from the code (`avoid::shank_hits`), and no pin turns it on.
- No Mac build. The builds and tests ran on winbuild only.

## Files

- `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/raster.rs` is now 406 lines. It was 410 lines on main. The seam hook adds lines, and `shallow_footprint` moved to `polar.rs` (369 lines), its only user. All new files are below 400 lines. No new test binary: the tests join the `multiaxis` and `start_exit_shared` suites.

title: fix(post): Sodick Mark 21 header names its control, warns LN1W/LN2W, states T91 threading
body:
## What changed

This PR changes the header comments and the `description` of `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` ("Sodick Wire EDM (Mark 21)"). No code line changes.

- The control line now names the control: `(SODICK MARK 21 / EX21 CONTROL WORDS - NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL - CHECK BEFORE CUTTING)`.
- A new line follows it in every program: `(LN1W/LN2W: NOT SUPPORTED - G21 ALARMS E00170 AND THE TAPER WORDS DIFFER - USE THE SODICK WIRE EDM LN2W POST)` (#4046).
- The threading line now matches the program (#4044):
  - With AWT: `(PROGRAM THREADS THE WIRE WITH T91 AT START)`.
  - Without AWT: `(WIRE NOT THREADED AT START - THE OPERATOR THREADS IT AT THE M00)`.
- The post `description` now reads: "Sodick wire EDM, 2-axis (Mark 21 / EX21 control, words from the 1998 operation manual; not verified on a control). LN1W/LN2W: not supported - G21 alarms (E00170) and the taper words differ - use the Sodick Wire EDM (LN2W) post". The text before the first " (" does not change. Thus `units::post_name` names the post in a refusal as before.

The G-code comment has no parentheses around `E00170` and `LN2W`. The first `)` ends a comment on the control. The description is not G-code, so it keeps the given wording.

## Cause

- #4046: the header said "MARK 21 WORDS" only. An LN2W owner read it as a post for their control. On LN2W, `G21` gives alarm `E00170`, and taper uses other words.
- #4044: the header said "WIRE NOT THREADED AT START". Some lines later the program writes `T91`, which threads the wire.

## Taper programs (#4046 "beside the first G74/G75")

This post writes no `G74`/`G75` and no taper words. It refuses a tapered or 4-axis section by name (`taper_and_four_axis_are_refused_by_name`, `sodick_taper.rs`). Thus no taper program exists to carry a second line. The header line is in every program, the refused ones too. The refusal messages do not change, because this PR changes only comments and the description. The decision file records this.

## Tests

- Pin: `camcraft-post` `sodick_dielectric::the_header_names_the_mark_21_control_warns_ln_owners_and_states_the_threading`. It checks the control line, the LN1W/LN2W line and the threading line before the first code line, with and without AWT. It also checks the description.
- Red before the fix: yes. On the unchanged post it fails at `sodick_dielectric.rs:218` ("`(SODICK MARK 21 / EX21 CONTROL WORDS ...)` missing").
- Mutation: the post from `upstream/main` put back gives red. The fixed post gives green (8 passed).

title: feat(post): report unchanged incoming stock deficits
body:
## Change

Allow a setup-session acknowledgment for a single upright setup that uses model stock marked as raw stock only. Compare the incoming and finished stock on the same simulation grid. Report the count, maximum depth and location of deficient cells that stay at their incoming heights. A new or deeper deficit still holds posting.

Opening the project clears the acknowledgment and keeps the raw-stock-only mark. The MCP tool `set_raw_stock_only` exposes the optional acknowledgment (`report_inherited_deficits`).

### Review fixes (`3c4e3b7b8`)

Two independent reviews of the first version found six cases. Each case has a pinning test that fails without its fix.

- A program of touch probes only plans nothing in the column simulation (#108). It was refused even with the acknowledgment. Now it is judged and noted the same way.
- A torch or a wire removes material that the column never sees (#670). An undercut pass lowers no column top (#1444). A program with one of these keeps the full gate, because unchanged tops cannot show that the program left a cell alone.
- A probe in a setup other than the judged one never uses that setup's acknowledgment.
- A program that cuts nothing was judged on the first setup's stock, wherever it ran. Now `carry::walk` takes its steps from the program's own operations when nothing is planned. The program is judged on the setup it runs in and crosses setups by the same entry law as a cutting program. Cutting programs walk exactly as before. **This changes the ordinary verdict (acknowledgment off) for programs of probes or torches only.**
- Across setups that the walk cannot cross (a later setup's model stock, a machine change), such a program now refuses by name in the not-judged arm. Before, it posted. The operations' generator verdicts judge paths, not stock.

## Readings

The synthetic fixture has a step 5 mm below the part surface. Posting holds before acknowledgment, passes with a located 5.00 mm note after acknowledgment, and holds again after reopening. A second cut that deepens the step by 3 mm still holds posting. A probe-only program behaves the same way on the stock of its own setup. A torch, a T-slot pass, or a probe in another setup keeps the hold. A two-setup probe or plasma program that the walk cannot cross is refused, and no NC file is written.

## Checks

- On `3c4e3b7b8`, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed 353 of 354 steps, with 0 stalled. The one failure was the golden comparison in `sinumerik_810m_post`. It read a stale CRLF working copy of the committed kit file `docs/tester-kits/sinumerik-810m-vmc200/air_cut_vmc200.mpf`, which is marked `eol=lf` and is not changed by this PR. After the copy was restored to the committed bytes (no diff), that suite passed 3 of 3.
- Clippy passed for all targets of `camcraft-app` with warnings denied.
- The 16 pinning tests are in the `keep_law` binary under `incoming_stock_deficits`. Twenty other suites on posting, probing, plasma and setups also passed: 179 of 179 tests in 21 suites on `3c4e3b7b8`.

The test setup uses synthetic stock on Windows. The light lane belongs to the independent upstream review. Full heavy lanes run at the release cut.

The fork synced at v0.26.0.

- A new post script, `assets/posts/sodick-ln2w.cps`, is in the registry as **Sodick Wire EDM (LN2W)**.
- It is a second `.cps` file beside the Mark 21 script. The post engine evaluates one script text and has no include, so the two scripts cannot share code. - `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` has no change. The Mark 21 output is byte-identical.

- The post writes no `G20` and no `G21`. It declares `programUnits = "mm"`, so the engine refuses an inch document by name.
- The post writes vertical 2-axis cuts only. It refuses each taper by name: a `WireTaper` section, an angle word, a U V lean. A taper (`TP` / `TN`, `G51` / `G52` `A`, `G50`) waits for #4075. See "Round 3" below.
- A skim pass takes `T85` (`edm.skim_flushing`) and its own `C` word.
- A new machine file, `assets/machines/sodick-aq600l.mch` (**Sodick AQ600L**), names the LN2W post as its default post. U/V travel is 80 x 80 mm. It states no `edm.taper_angle`.

- The guides and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describe the new post.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/4045-sodick-ln2w-dialect.md`.

### Round 3 (review of head `b12db2f06`, and the owner's correction)

| Finding | What changed |
|---|---|
| 1. U/V travel 120 mm | U/V is 80 x 80 mm (+-40), from the brochure that the review cites. The example guide span is 100 mm: a 20 degree lean is 36.4 mm, inside the 40 mm half travel. The profile test checks both. |
| 2. `mitre` corners with no evidence | The file states no `edm.taper_angle`. The post refuses each tapered cut, so no cut depends on a corner rule. |
| 3. `top_right` leans to the wrong side | No `G51` / `G52` is written. A taper on a `top_right` machine, with a positive or a negative angle, is refused by name. A regression case pins it. |
| 4. One fixture height for each setup | `edm.table_to_part_bottom` and `PARAM WireBottom` are removed (they were this PR's own). No `TP` / `TN` is written. The taper waits for a setup height (#4075). |
| 5. STEP bench skips `edm/` | `step_agreement` reads `testdata/models/edm/`, has three rows and three tests. A new STEP subdirectory that no bench pins fails the file-set test. `edge_gap/` is named as the `step_edge_gap` bench's. |
| 6. 0.0004 degree posts as `A0.` | No `A` word is written. A 0.0004 degree taper is refused by name. A regression case pins it. |
| Optional: pin path in `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` | It names `crates/post/tests/sodick_ln2w/pins.rs` and the binary `script_sodick_ln2w`. |
| Owner: `U0. V0.` on the rapid | `startCut` writes `G00 X Y U0. V0.`. The header comment and the guide state the new order. |

### Each hunk in an existing file

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `crates/app/src/posting.rs`, `posting_files.rs` | Register the post and the machine file. |
| `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`, `machine.rs`, `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs` | List tests that the new post and the new machine must join. |

The Sodick post writes the Mark 21 word set. The LN2W control of the AQ600L alarms on `G21` (`E00170`) and needs a different start order.

## Sources

- The statements of the owner of a Sodick AQ600L (LN2W), relayed on #4045, #1500 and this PR.
- The Sodick LN1W / LN2W operation manual (2012), as this repository already records it (#4045, #1500, the decisions #1496, #1497, #2649, #2686). This session could not open the PDF: the web request was blocked.

title: feat(geometry): expand DXF blocks (INSERT) on import
body:
## What changed

The DXF reader now expands each `INSERT` of a `BLOCK` into world geometry. Before this PR, an `INSERT` was skipped and counted, and a user `BLOCK` definition stopped the import.

- The reader keeps the text of each block body. At EOF it reads a body once, when an `INSERT` uses it.
- An `INSERT` places its block by `at + R(rotation) S (p - base)`. Z goes by `at_z + sz (z - base_z)`.
- A column and row array (groups 70, 71, 44, 45) places one copy for each cell, along the turned and unscaled block axes.
- Nested blocks compose their transforms.
- A line maps exactly. Under a similarity (equal X and Y scale, any rotation), a circle stays a circle and an arc stays an arc, with exact centre, radius and angles.
- A mirror (one negative scale) reverses the arc: the arc keeps its drawn ends and runs clockwise.
- An exact similarity matrix is needed for the exact circle path. A near similarity takes the ellipse path below (review of the head `87cd87d0e`).
- A SPLINE or ELLIPSE in a block is fitted after its placement, in world units. The body keeps the curve definition, and each placed copy maps it exactly (review of the head `87cd87d0e`).
- Under unequal scales, a circle or an arc becomes an ellipse. The reader lays it with the #3958 ELLIPSE fit: tangent arcs within `CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM` (1 µm, two-sided). The tolerance is recorded on the document.
- Block geometry on layer `0` takes the layer of its `INSERT` (the DXF rule), also through nested inserts. The chainer joins only primitives on the same layer, so this geometry chains with the top-level geometry of that layer. The 2D DXF flow and the wire chain flow need no change.
- TEXT, MTEXT, DIMENSION, HATCH and POINT in a block are skipped and counted, as at top level. Text in a block is not kept as an annotation.

The decision file is `docs/decisions/1865-dxf-insert.md`.

## Bounds and refusals

- Each copy and each placed primitive counts against the vertex limit (`Limits::max_vertices`, 1 000 000 by default). A nested array of empty blocks cannot hang the import.
- An array with more copies than that limit is refused before any work.
- Nesting is bounded by `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH` = 8 levels.
- These are refused by name (the `INSERT` or `BLOCK` name is in the message):
  - a cyclic or self reference;
  - a block that is not defined (before this PR such an `INSERT` was skipped);
  - nesting past 8 levels;
  - an array count below 1;
  - a scale of zero, or a scale outside 1e-9 to 1e9 in size;
  - a non-finite value;
  - an extrusion that is not +Z, a thickness, paper space;
  - an external reference block (flag 4 or 8);
  - a duplicate block name (names ignore case);
  - a `BLOCK` without `ENDBLK`;
  - placed geometry outside the coordinate range;
  - a block whose Z plane differs from the drawing's.
- Bad geometry in a used block is refused with the block name first (`BLOCK A: LINE: zero-length entity`).
- A block that no `INSERT` uses is not read. Thus a bad or cyclic block that is never placed does not stop the import.

## Review fixes (head `87cd87d0e` review)

1. Tolerance after the complete INSERT transform. Before, a block SPLINE or ELLIPSE was fitted in block units, and the placement scaled the fit error. Now a block body keeps each SPLINE and ELLIPSE as its definition (`insert_curve.rs`, new). Each placed copy maps the ellipse centre and axis vectors, or the spline control points, by the affine map of the whole INSERT chain. Then it fits the curve in world units within `CURVE_TOLERANCE_MM`. The reviewer's ELLIPSE (ratio 0.99995, scale 100) now gives tangent arcs within 1 µm of the true ellipse.
2. Similarity shortcut bounded in drawing units. The shortcut to an exact circle now needs an exact matrix (`a == d && b == -c`, or the mirror form). Equal scales give exact entries, also when nested transforms compose them. A near similarity takes the ellipse path, which measures `major - minor` in drawing units against the tolerance and records the tolerance. The reviewer's case (radius 1000, scales 1e8 and 1e8 + 5e-5) is refused by name: `INSERT: curve is too long for its tolerance within the import budget`.

The top-level SPLINE and ELLIPSE paths of #3958 fit in drawing units, with no transform after the fit. The only later scale is the unit scale, and `SketchData::from_document` already refuses a tolerance that the unit makes looser than 1 µm (`sketch_data.rs:115`).

New pinning tests, `dxf` binary, `block_curves` (a new submodule of the existing `dxf` directory suite):
- `a_scaled_near_round_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units` (the reviewer's repro)
- `a_nested_scaled_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units` (two levels, scale 10 x 10, turned 30 degrees)
- `an_unequally_scaled_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units`
- `a_scaled_spline_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units` (equal, unequal and mirrored scales)
- `a_nested_scaled_spline_keeps_the_bound_in_world_units`
- `a_near_similarity_is_no_exact_circle` (the reviewer's repro)
- `a_near_similarity_within_the_tolerance_records_it`

Each test samples 4001 points of the exact affine image of the drawn curve, checks each point within 1 µm (1 % slack) of the output, checks `curve_tolerance == Some(0.001)`, and checks that the pieces join.

Mutations (each undone after the run):
- Block curves not deferred (`defer_curves` kept `false` in `Expansion::body`): 5 tests red (all ellipse and spline tests of `block_curves`).
- The old relative threshold `1e-12 * max|entry|` restored in `Affine::similarity`: `a_near_similarity_is_no_exact_circle` red.
- Before the fix, all 6 first tests were red on `87cd87d0e` (for example 0.05 mm at the minor end of the reviewer's ellipse).

## Readings

- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/insert.rs` (new): `INSERT` record, block definitions, expansion and bounds.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/insert_place.rs` (new): the affine map and the placement of one primitive.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/insert_curve.rs` (new): block SPLINE and ELLIPSE definitions, placed exactly and fitted after the placement.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/nurbs.rs`: `Nurbs::mapped` maps the control points.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/curves.rs`: the tail of the ELLIPSE fit is now `ellipse_arcs`, and the SPLINE fit is `spline_arcs`, both shared with the placement. A block body defers its curves. The top-level output does not change.
- `crates/geometry/src/dxf/reader.rs`, `blocks.rs`, `types.rs`, `mod.rs`: the entity loop also reads a block body; non-layout blocks go to the definitions; expansion at EOF.

## Pinning tests

Geometry (`camcraft-geometry`):
- `dxf` binary, `blocks::insert_moves_turns_and_scales_a_block_keeping_arcs_exact`
- `blocks::a_mirrored_insert_reverses_the_arc`

- `blocks::nested_blocks_compose_and_layer_zero_takes_the_insert_layer` (3 levels)
- `blocks::a_block_reference_that_was_skipped_now_reads_its_block`
- `dxf_refusals` binary, `block_refusals::cyclic_missing_and_too_deep_blocks_are_refused_by_name`
- `block_refusals::copy_counts_past_the_vertex_limit_are_refused_without_the_work`

- `block_refusals::mutated_block_records_never_panic` (fixed-seed mutation loop, 300 cases)

App (`camcraft-app`):
- `wire_dxf_selection` binary, `arcs::an_inserted_block_cuts_and_posts_like_the_same_top_level_circle`: a circle in a nested block, inserted at half scale and turned, on layer `0` under an `INSERT` on `outline`. It posts byte for byte the program of the golden `wire-iso/wire_dxf_die_circle.nc` (two G3 blocks with I J).
- `arcs::arcs_stay_refused_for_taper_and_a_hatch_still_blocks_the_cut`: an `INSERT` of a missing block is now refused at import, by name.

title: fix(multiaxis): start and exit picks for the multi-axis contour
body:
## What changed

The Multi-Axis Contour (`OpType::MultiAxisContour`, the drive-curve planner `multiaxis::contour_curve`) takes a start point and an exit point. This is slice 2 of #3330. Slice 1 (the 5-Axis Contour) is PR #4006.

The title uses `fix`: the issue has the `bug` label, and PR #4028 used `fix` for the same reason.

Behaviour (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve_seam.rs`, hook in `contour_curve_seamed`):

- Each pick acts on the drive curve nearest it. The other curves keep their automatic cut. The cut order of the curves does not change.
- A pick with a Z is read in 3D. A pick without a Z is read in XY.
- Closed curve, start: the curve starts at its point nearest the pick. A foot between two vertices becomes a new vertex on that segment.
- Closed curve, exit: the curve cuts its full lap from its seam. Then it runs on along its own points to its point nearest the exit pick, and the tool leaves there.
- Open curve: the start pick selects the end where the cut starts (the nearer end). The exit pick selects the end where the cut leaves. The direction of the curve can reverse.
- The re-sequence occurs before the walk. Thus the rest law, the tilt limit (`command_axis` in the max-tilt cone) and the shank dodge judge each station of the picked path, as on the automatic path. The app's centre-cut audit (`audit_posed`) and the verify pass also read the picked path.
- The kind has no leads, so there is no lead-room law.
- With no pick, `apply` returns before it touches the curves. The path is byte-identical.
- `PickCapability::Ring` for the kind. The MCP `edit_operation` schema says how the kind reads a pick.

## Refusals (by name, before any motion)

- `start point (x, y): the nearest drive curve stands D mm away, farther than R mm (1.5 tool diameters) - ...` (also for the exit).
- `start point (...): drive curve N is open and its cut can start only at an end; its nearest end (...) stands D mm away, farther than R mm - ...` (also for the exit: `leave only at an end`).
- `exit point (...): it is nearer the end of open drive curve N where the start point begins the cut - ...`.
- `start point (...): the plunge column over drive curve N at (x, y, z) crosses the part - ...` and `exit point (...): the retract column over drive curve N at (...) crosses the part - ...`. The column law sweeps the ball up the vertical line to the hop plane, every 0.25 mm, and it checks the shank at each step when shank avoidance is on.

## Mutations

Each mutation was applied alone, the pins were run, and the source was restored.

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `curve_seam::rotate` keeps the automatic seam (start seat off) | RED: `curve_start_point_seats_a_closed_curve_at_the_pick`, `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick`, `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M2 | `run_on`: the full lap dropped (the exit becomes a chord) | RED: `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick` |
| M3 | the plunge column check off (`curve.rs`) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | the retract column check off (`curve.rs`) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | open curve: the start reversal off | RED: `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends`, `curve_pick_acts_on_its_nearest_curve_only`, `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`; app: `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name` |
| M6 | open curve: the exit reversal off | RED: `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends` |
| M7 | the same-end exit refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M8 | the open start end reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M9 | the open exit end reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M10 | the curve reach refusal off | RED: `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name` |
| M11 | the column sweep reads only the station (no samples up the column) | RED: `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name` |
| A1 | the app arm passes an empty seam | RED: `multiaxis_contour_starts_and_leaves_at_the_picked_ends`, `multiaxis_contour_refuses_impossible_picks_by_name` |
| A3 | the kind's capability back to `PICK_OWED` | RED: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick`, `multiaxis_contour_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` |

## Readings

- The pins that say "the cut geometry does not change" sample each cut move every 0.25 mm in both directions. Each sample of the picked path must be within 0.02 mm of the automatic ball-centre path (no chord, no gouge). Each sample of the automatic path must be within 0.02 mm of the picked path (no part of the curve left uncut). The walk's chord budget is 0.0025 mm.
- Box 40 x 40 x 15, ring at z = 7.5, ball r = 3: the start pick (20, -1) gives a first ball centre at (20.0, -3.0, 7.5) within 0.05 mm. The exit pick (-1, 20) gives a last ball centre at (-3.0, 20.0, 7.5).
- A canopy slab at z 18 to 20 above the middle of the y = 0 wall: a pick under it is refused for the plunge and for the retract. A pick on the x = 0 wall cuts.

## Pinning tests

- motion `multiaxis` (module `curve_seam`): `curve_start_point_seats_a_closed_curve_at_the_pick`, `curve_exit_point_carries_a_closed_curve_on_to_the_pick`, `curve_picks_on_an_open_curve_select_its_ends`, `curve_pick_acts_on_its_nearest_curve_only`, `curve_impossible_picks_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_picked_columns_under_a_canopy_are_refused_by_name`, `curve_without_a_pick_is_the_automatic_path_byte_for_byte`.

- No new top-level test binary: the new files are modules of `multiaxis` and `start_exit_shared`.

## Goldens moved

None expected. No `*.nc`, `*.cl` or `examples/catalog/**` file changed.

## Not exercised

- A pick on a shank-avoid path where the shank, not the ball, blocks the column. The shank step uses the existing `shank_hits_at`; no pin drives it.
- A closed drive curve through the application (the app pins use the box's four open top edges). The closed curve is pinned at motion scale.
- A setup with a rotated frame: the picks and the drive curves are both in the setup frame, as for the 5-Axis Contour.

## Code shape

- `curve.rs` had 860 lines. Its unit tests moved, unchanged, to `curve_tests.rs`. It now has 719 lines, with the hook. A further split is a follow-up.
- No new crate edge.

## Remaining kinds of #3330

Parallel5D, Swarf, AdvancedSwarf, RotaryContour, RotaryParallel, RotaryOffset, MultiAxisRough, Flow5D.

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 216 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.3 min). The plan includes `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: multiaxis`, `motion suites: pivot5d`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `center_cut_multiaxis`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (14.4 min).

title: fix(mcp): release the ui link owner lock by unlock, not by a close
body:
## Cause

The post-merge gate of `3bb6647f6` failed in `mcp_live`, test `ui_link_owner::a_false_server_that_proves_the_token_gets_no_tool_call_when_the_window_has_ended`. The cause is a race between a lock release by a close and a concurrent child process start. Part of it is in the product code of #3995 (PR #4020), and not only in the test.

- On Unix, a `flock` belongs to the open file, not to the descriptor.
- When a thread starts a child process (`Command::spawn`), the child holds a copy of each descriptor until its `exec` closes it.
- A close of the lock file during that time does not release the lock.
- `mcp_live` runs many tests in parallel, and some of them start `camcraft-cli` children. Thus the race occurs often in that binary.

The two places:

1. **Product code**: `link_owner::owner`. To prove that a window has ended, it takes the free lock and released it only by the close of the file. When a fork occurred at that moment, the lock stayed held. The next lock test then read the ended window as alive, and the CLI dialed its address. This is the defect class that #3995 closes. In a looped run, the CLI dialed the false server of the crashed-window test (`Busy` after the hello timeout).
2. **Test code**: the tests ended a stand-in window with `drop(lock)`. The CLI's lock test after the hello then saw the lock still held, opened a session and sent the tool call to the false server. The failure text was `Failed("... closed the link before it answered")` at `ui_link_owner.rs:111`.

## What changed

- `link_owner::owner`: after it takes a free lock, it calls `File::unlock` before the close. If the unlock fails, the entry is unproved and is not dialed.
- `Registration::drop` (a window closes): unlocks after it removed its files.
- `link::open`: unlocks on the bind-error path.
- Tests: the new helper `release_lock` ends a stand-in window with an unlock, as the OS does at a process end. Both `ui_link_owner` tests that end a window use it.

No retry, no sleep and no `#[ignore]`. Decision record: `docs/decisions/4041-ui-link-lock-release.md`.

Residual (in the decision record): when a window process crashes while one of its own threads starts a child, the lock stays held until that child runs `exec`. This is a short time, and the OS ends it.

## Readings

Loop: the whole `mcp_live` binary (25 tests), `--test-threads=24` as on the runner, four loops at the same time for load, from `crates/app`:

- Unchanged binary (`origin/main` `3bb6647f6` tree): 150 runs. `a_false_server_that_proves_the_token_gets_no_tool_call_when_the_window_has_ended` failed in 42 runs. `a_crashed_windows_file_is_removed_and_its_port_is_never_dialed` failed in 2 runs. (These runs used a copy of the binary with no `assets/` beside it, so `live_gate_allows_explicitly_approved_calls_and_never_auto_approves_post_or_machine_edits` also failed in all 150. That is an artifact of the copy, not a result.)
- Test fix only (the product code unchanged): 200 runs, 1 failure. `a_crashed_windows_file_is_removed_and_its_port_is_never_dialed` returned `Busy`: the CLI dialed the false server. This showed the product defect in `owner`.
- Final head (the test fix and the product fix): **200 of 200 runs passed**, in place, with no failure in any test.

Gate on the final head:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 3 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (app build, app lib, `mcp_live`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Pinning tests: `ui_link_owner::a_false_server_that_proves_the_token_gets_no_tool_call_when_the_window_has_ended` and `ui_link_owner::a_crashed_windows_file_is_removed_and_its_port_is_never_dialed`, pinned by the 200-run loop.
- Light lane: not run. The diff does not reach the light twins (motion adaptive twins and `pocket_pass_start`), and it changes no post and no toolpath. No heavy step: this is a P2 PR.

## Not exercised

- Windows and macOS were not run. On Windows, `LockFileEx` belongs to the handle, and std makes handles non-inheritable. The explicit unlock is correct there too.
- A crash of a real window process during a child start was not emulated (see the residual).

title: docs(process): the Side branch rule for side/path-kernel
body:
## What changed

- `AGENTS.md`: a new rule **Side branch** in "Issue Law", directly after **Overlapping issues stack**. The two rules are about a PR whose base is not `main`, so a reader finds them together. "Pull Request Law" gets only short pointers to the rule.
- `AGENTS.md`: three small edits remove contradictions with the new rule:
  - **Start from the latest main**: a new sub-bullet "A sub-PR of a side branch starts from that branch (**Side branch**)."
  - **Done on a branch**: a new sentence "A sub-PR of a side branch uses `--base side/<name>` and `Refs #N`, and its issue keeps `in-review` after the merge (**Side branch**)."
  - **When PRs merge**: a new sentence "Never use `--delete-branch` on a PR whose head is a side branch."
  - **When a PR merges**: a new sentence "A sub-PR of a side branch is the exception (**Side branch**)."
- `.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md`: step 1 uses `origin/side/path-kernel` for a sub-PR. Step 5 gives the base, the body start line, `Refs #N` and the gate base for a sub-PR.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`: the switch-over PR merges only on the maintainer's word and without `--delete-branch`. A sub-PR keeps its `side/*` base (no retarget to `main`). After a sub-PR merge, its issue keeps `in-review` and gets the fixed comment.
- `docs/decisions/4042-side-branch-rule.md`: the decisions of this PR.

## The new rule, in full

```
- **Side branch** (#4023, #4042). A side branch `side/<name>` collects the
  sub-PRs of one large change. Then one PR takes it to `main`. Only the
  maintainer permits a side branch. `side/path-kernel` is the one that
  exists. It is made from `main` after this rule merges. Its plan is in
  `docs/decisions/4024-path-kernel-design.md`.
  - The branch is protected against a force-push and a deletion. It is
    never rebased. Each change goes to it through a sub-PR.
  - A sub-PR has one issue. Its worktree is made from `origin/side/<name>`,
    on a branch `issue/N-<slug>`. It opens as a draft with `--base
    side/<name>`.
  - The body of a sub-PR starts with `Side branch: side/<name>`. It ends
    with `Refs #N`, not `Fixes #N`: a merge into a side branch closes no
    issue.
  - A sub-PR gets the quick pass and the collaborator review as each other
    PR. It merges with a merge commit when its review is clean, also as a
    `feat`. `--delete-branch` deletes only the sub-PR's own branch.
  - The issue of a merged sub-PR keeps `in-review` until the switch-over PR
    merges. The merging session comments `merged to side/<name> in PR #M;
    closes at the switch-over` on the issue.
  - `main` is merged into the side branch with `git merge`, through a sync
    PR into the side branch. Never rebase, never force-push. Do this after
    each merge batch on `main` that touches the code of the side branch,
    and at least each week. If the two sides changed the same logic, the
    sync stops and the maintainer decides (`resolve-conflicts` skill).
  - The gates are local: `post-merge.yml` covers `main` only. Each sub-PR
    runs its pinning tests, the quick gate of its diff against
    `origin/side/<name>`, the example catalog suites and the light lane.
    The head of the side branch gets one local batch gate after each sync,
    inside the build limit. A red batch is fixed on the side branch before
    the next sub-PR merges.
  - The lane and in-flight limits count a sub-PR as each other PR.
  - The switch-over is one PR from `side/<name>` to `main`. It lists
    `Fixes #N` for each issue that it closes. It merges only on the
    maintainer's word: an agent review is not enough. It merges without
    `--delete-branch`.
```

## Decisions

- Place: in "Issue Law" after **Overlapping issues stack**, not in "Pull Request Law". The reason is above.
- A sub-PR that is a `feat` merges into the side branch when its review is clean. The feat-at-cut rule applies to the switch-over PR to `main`.
- The protection text names only what the maintainer approved: no force-push and no deletion.

## Tests

Docs and process files only. No build and no gate ran: the diff has no code.

Not exercised: the steps on a real `side/path-kernel` branch. The branch does not exist yet; the coordinator makes it after this PR merges.

body:
Stacked on #4022. Own commit: `bea85a429` (the one feature commit of this PR). The other commits are merge commits: `c7934501f` and `2f6476301` merge the #4022 branch (now at `87805dcf9`), and `65ec94c5c` merges `origin/main` at `aef12fea6`. Retarget this PR to `main` before #4022 merges.

## Behaviour

- A Wire Contour with the side **Die** on one selected closed DXF chain now posts through the Agie Wire EDM (AgieVision) post. Before this change, the post refused it ("reads a selected DXF chain only for a captured punch").
- The ISO keeps the nominal walls. It starts at the seam and runs counter-clockwise, with `G01`, `G02` and `G03` blocks and incremental `I`/`J` centres. A clockwise drawing is reversed.
- The SBL and SBR are the zero-step die setup of #2957 (`c_die`). Only the stem, the stock and the hole change.
- The control makes the lead, the passes and the separation. CamCraft writes no lead.
- The app reads the placed walls with the code of the inspection export (#3219). That code is now shared in `crates/app/src/operation/agie_opening.rs`. The inspection export keeps its behaviour.
- The ordinary Wire Contour generator and the wire laws still judge the generated kerf before the native post runs.
- New: `crates/post/src/agie/opening.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/opening/walls.rs` (exact distances between lines and arcs), `examples/agie/reentrant-die.{dxf,camscript}`, a user guide section and `docs/decisions/3178-agie-reentrant-opening.md`.

## Rules and refusals

Each rule uses the rough offset of the 20 mm QN2 row (0.245 mm). Each refusal names the rule and its values.

| Rule | Refusal starts with | Control evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Joints and arc centres on the 0.00001 mm grid, equal squared radii at both arc ends | `Native arc radius rule` (both radii) | `RADB` (0.001 mm difference): the control moved the centre by half the difference. `RADA` (0.003 mm): no plotted path, no message. |
| An inside fillet of the plate (a CCW arc of the CCW opening) has a radius larger than 0.245 mm | `Native arc offset rule` (radius, offset) | `FILR` (R0.2): FORMALCHECK passed, but the Main pass left the arc out and cut a sharp corner. The control does not refuse it. CamCraft refuses it. |
| An arc joins its neighbours tangentially; only two straight walls meet at a sharp corner | `Native joint rule` (the point) | `REENT20`: the sharp tooth tips got round R0.245 turns. |
| A sharp inside corner of the plate leaves at most 0.002 mm | `Strict cover rule` (angle, rest) | Same law as the polygon die. |
| Walls that are not neighbours are more than 2 × (corner reach + 0.245) apart | `The walls from … are … mm apart` | Conservative bound. |
| Hole inside, more than 1 mm from each wall; straight entry wall parallel to X or Y; 3 mm lead and 3 mm of wall each side; lead 0.4 mm clear of other walls | hole and entry texts | `REENT20`: straight lead from the hole to the seam. |
| 0.4 mm of stock beyond each wall and arc extremum; 20 mm plate | stock texts | Same as the polygon die. |

"Tangent entry radius larger than the offset" does not apply: CamCraft writes no arc lead.

## Imported on an offline copy of the control's software (2026-11-25)

- `REENT20` (unmodified output of `examples/agie/reentrant-die.camscript`):
  - The ISO and SBL arrived byte for byte. The tree showed `CCB030[0]`.
  - One formal error before TECCUT ("Technologie : te definiëren"). TECCUT row 0199 (Dia 0.25, H20, Ra 0.30) was assigned. The tree showed `CCB030[4]`, offsets 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.
  - FORMALCHECK: no errors. Only the two usual warnings.
  - Plot: the Main pass runs counter-clockwise 0.245 mm inside the opening. The fillets became concentric arcs of r − 0.245. The clockwise R4 tongue tip became a concentric `G02` of R4.245. The Main pass ends 1 mm before the seam. The trims run reversed.
- `FILR`, `RADA` and `RADB` are the same job with one hand edit of the ISO each. CamCraft refuses those edits.

N0005 and N0009 are the tooth fillets. N0006 to N0008 are the tooth. N0013 and N0017 are the tongue fillets. N0015 is the R4 tongue tip (G02 about X0 Y4). N0022 returns to the seam.

title: fix(mcp): list every accepted field of a kind in list_operation_types
body:
## What changed

Before this change, `list_operation_types` listed only the fields that the default params serialize. Agents did not find optional fields (pocket `tilt` and `rest`, the plasma `feed` and pierce keys, the Wire Contour extras). Enum fields showed only `"string"`.

- New module `crates/app/src/mcp/kind_fields.rs` with `kind_fields/trace.rs`. The trace runs the `Deserialize` of `ParamsDto` with a recording deserializer. It records the struct field names, the enum variant names and the `Option` fields of each kind. One rule applies to all kinds. The PR adds no hand list of field names.
- Each field row now has these additions:
  - `"optional": true` when the defaults do not write the field.
  - `"values"` for an enum field (for example drill `cycle`, pocket `entry` and `strategy`, wire `side`).
  - `"shape"` for an object or array field (for example `rest`, `tilt`, `tabs`, `links`). A `key?` in the shape is optional.
- Two kinds flatten a struct (`#[serde(flatten)]`): `thread` and `sinker_side_burn`. Serde gives no key names for such a struct. Thus `kind_fields::flattened` traces the flattened type by itself, and it names the six optional keys of the thread variant.
- A second small trace (`kind_fields/written.rs`, a recording serializer) gives the keys that the kind's params can write. A key that the type reads but never writes (`#[serde(skip_serializing)]`) is not offered. Example: the legacy wire `start`, which the load migrates into `picks`.
- A kind that the trace cannot read gets `"fields_incomplete": true`. The pinning test fails on it.
- The note of the tool tells what the new keys mean.
- `job.rs` gets 5 more lines (it was already over 400). The new logic is in the new module.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3449-list-op-type-fields.md`.

## Readings

- Each kind is traced. Only the height fields (`retract_z`, `bottom_z`, face `top_z`) have the type `"any"`, because `HeightDto` reads itself (untagged).
- The reply for one kind stays below the 4000-character budget. Measured replies: pocket 3604, sinker_side_burn 2123, wire_contour 2009, thread 1924, drill 1834, plasma_profile 1681, face 1563.

## Pinning tests

- `op_type_fields::list_operation_types_reads_every_kind_completely` (binary `mcp`, new file `crates/app/tests/mcp/op_type_fields.rs` in the `tests/mcp/` directory suite). This is the Done clause: every kind is traced, no kind is incomplete, and no field is listed twice.
- `op_type_fields::list_operation_types_names_the_optional_fields_and_enum_words`: pocket `tilt`/`rest`/`entry`, the Wire Contour extras and `tabs` shape, the plasma `feed`/`kerf`/`pierce_*`/`cut_height`, the drill `cycle` words, and the thread pass keys.
- The existing pins also pass: `mcp_wire_contour::list_operation_types_and_skill_match_wire_contour_dto_and_tool_law` (the wire fields are the same as the DTO keys), `mcp_wire_contour::list_operation_types_says_the_wire_kind_mounts_a_wire_tool`, `mcp_compact::list_operation_types_filters_by_kind_and_by_section` (4000-character budget), `break_through::issue_2441_mcp_list_operation_types_lists_break_through`.
- The pinning test also checks that the wire listing does not offer the legacy `start`.

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick` on the final head (Linux, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`): 1215 steps, 1212 pass, 3 fail, 0 stall. All app, motion, kernel, post, sim and gpu steps pass. The 3 failed steps are UI steps that need a wgpu adapter. This host has no display and no `xvfb-run`:
  - `ui suites: lib`: `egui_app::report_tests::*` and `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds` panic with `Failed to create render state: CustomNativeAdapterSelectionError("No adapter found")`.
  - `ui suites: egui_app` (3 headless start tests) and `ui suites: shell` (`headless_cli_exit_code_is_zero`): the headless run returns 1 for the same reason.
  - This PR changes no UI file. A runner with a display must run these 3 steps again.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- Serde cannot see a new optional key on the outer `thread` variant (a variant with a flatten), and the test does not find it. That one list of six names is written by hand.
- Wire `condition` is required by the add_operation check, not by serde. The listing shows it as an optional field with the default `""`, as before. It does not mark it as required.
- The issue asks for a unit for each field. Serde has no unit, so this PR does not add units.
- Light lane and heavy lanes: not run. No post or toolpath changed, and this is a P3 PR.
- PR #4007 touches other files (UI and `tests/mcp_rotary_flow.rs`). No overlap.

title: fix(adaptive): a 2D Adaptive takes a start point and an exit point
body:
## What changed

The 2D Adaptive (`Adaptive2D`) takes a start point and an exit point (slice of #1448). The picks are the shared operation-level `picks` field of #3339. The command, the project file, the stamp and MCP `edit_operation` need no change.

- `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`: `Adaptive2D` is now `PickCapability::Region`. Only the Adaptive2D arm changes. The door refusal of the settings that cannot hold a pick is added to `pick_refusal`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_picks.rs` (new): the door (`adaptive_pick_refusal`), the picked entry, the piece order, the refusals, and the exit run back on the posted path (`exit_on_path`).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_hsm.rs`: `choose_entry` uses the start point as the seed. The pieces are ordered by `order_pieces`. A picked plan that falls back to the rings, or that keeps an overload, is refused by name. The budget unit test moves to `pocket_hsm_ring.rs` (the same test, so that the file stays under 400 lines).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs`: one hook after `emit_pocket_passes` for the exit.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_avoid.rs`: a pick in a "Do not touch" keep-out is refused with the item names.
- `crates/motion/src/approach.rs`: two runtime fields, `start_point` and `exit_point`. They are not saved. `crates/app/src/operation/adaptive_pick_op.rs` (new) lays the op's picks over the generation copy, or refuses them.
- `crates/app/src/operation/wcs_yaw.rs`: under a Z-rotated work offset the Adaptive picks turn into the generation frame, as the Slot picks do.
- UI: the Lead in / Lead out tab of the 2D Adaptive draws the Start point and Exit point groups (`start_exit_rows::region_groups`, drawn from `op_page.rs` because `mill2d_page.rs` is already over 400 lines). The viewport pick and the marks take the 2D Adaptive.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3327-adaptive-start-exit.md`.

## The law

- Start: the start point is the seed of the HSM plan. The helix (or the plunge) goes down there on each level, through the same entry law and the same triangle room as the automatic seed. The planner then grows the cleared area from that bore and measures each cut on its stock.
- Exit: the last pass of each level ends where the plan ends, on its closing ride along the walls. Then the tool runs back along the same posted moves in reverse (one round of the outer wall at most) to the point nearest the exit point, and climbs out there. A reversed line is the same line and a reversed arc is the same arc, so the run back cuts no new material and makes no feed-feed crossing. The piece nearest the exit point is cut last.
- The cut geometry does not change otherwise. Without a pick no new code runs.

## Refusals (by name, the pick is never moved, nothing is cut)

- `the start point (x, y) is outside the area the tool centre can reach ...`
- `the helix of radius r has no room at the start point (x, y) - the tool centre has c mm of room there and the helix needs n ...` (the plan's own 0.6 helix share)
- `the start|exit point (x, y) is inside the 'Do not touch' keep-out of <names> ...`
- `the exit point (x, y) is d mm from the closing ride of the last pass along the walls - the most is L ...` (L = 1.5 tool diameters + stock to leave, the contour's reach law)
- `the exit point ... is at the piece of the area where the cut starts, and n other piece(s) are cut after it ...`
- `an exit point needs the tool to climb out after the last pass of each level ...` (a level link that stays down)
- `the plan from the start point does not hold the optimal load (<planner note>) ...`
- `the HSM plan <reason> - the Offset rings or the trochoid that would cut the area instead do not take a start or exit point ...`
- At the door and at generation: a tilted (3+2) op, the Trochoidal method, Pass starts at Inside or Outside, a rest pass, and a start point with a Ramp or Arc entry.

## Readings

On a rectangle 60 x 40, tool D10, helix R2 (motion fixture):

- Automatic seed (30, 20): widest cut on the shape-mask meter 1.62 mm. Start point (15, 12): 1.79 mm. The limit in the test is 2.03 mm (the optimal load step with the plan's margin and the grid's).
- Start points (20, 15), (25, 20), (15, 12) are taken. A start point at (40, 25) makes the spiral keep "the least overload": it is refused. A start point at (12, 12) makes the plan cross itself: it is refused with that reason.
- Exit point (58, 20): each level ends at (55, 20). `crossed_pairs` is empty. The first try (a run back on the planner's walk, before the arc fit) read two crossings between the two arc fits, so the run back is made on the posted moves.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_levels` (`adaptive_picks` module):
  - `the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level` (two levels, no overload note, no crossing, widest cut under the limit)
  - `the_exit_point_is_where_the_last_pass_ends_on_each_level` (two levels, no crossing)
  - `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`
- `camcraft-app` `start_exit_shared` (`adaptive` module):
  - `the_entry_is_at_the_start_point_and_the_last_pass_ends_at_the_exit_point` (golden CL `adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl`)
  - `the_picks_hold_under_a_90_degree_wcs_yaw`
  - `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name_and_nothing_is_cut` (also the door: tilt, Trochoidal, Pass starts at Inside, Ramp entry)
  - `the_picks_ride_the_command_undo_the_file_and_the_stamp` (undo restores the previous path to the move; no pick plans the earlier path to the move)
  - `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_adaptive_picks` (`edit_operation`, `get_job` reads them back, `undo` clears them, `list_operation_types` says `start: true, exit: true`)
  - `the_2d_adaptive_takes_a_start_and_an_exit_point`, and `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated)
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `the_2d_adaptive_lead_tab_has_both_point_groups_and_takes_an_exit`, `a_2d_adaptive_takes_the_viewport_pick_and_shows_its_marks`

New test files join existing suites (`pass_start_levels/`, `start_exit_shared/`). No new top-level test binary.

## Goldens moved

None. One golden is new: `crates/app/tests/golden/adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl`. A path without a pick runs no new code (see the gate: `golden_cl`, the example catalog suites).

## Not exercised

- The keep-out refusal has no pinning fixture. The code is one `contains` test on the keep-out region that `adaptive_spiral_avoid_on` already builds.
- The "climb out" refusal (a level link that stays down) and the "exit at the start's piece" refusal have no fixture.
- A plunge entry at a start point is taken by the door. Its first turn out of a tool-size bore is the planner's existing note, not an overload refusal; no fixture.
- The Trochoidal method stays refused (its seed is on the medial line). #3932 (the trochoidal entry slots to a wall) is a separate path; this PR does not change it.
- No machine run.

## Why `fix`

The issue is labelled `bug` (the 2D Adaptive refused a start and an exit point that #1448 says it takes), and the earlier slice of the same family (#3325, the Slot) shipped as `fix(slot)`. So this PR is a `fix` too, and it merges when it is reviewed.

## Gate

All on the final head `3764e7ed9` (the branch with `origin/main` merged in; one conflict in `start_exit_shared.rs`, where #3981 and this PR each added lines to the gate map and to one assertion; both kept), local Mac, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=8`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 875 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (83.3 min). The plan includes `motion suites: pass_start_levels`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `golden_cl`, `ui suites: lib`, and the example catalog suites by name: `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` (all ok).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (14.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the code head before the merge of main (the merge changed only test lines in `start_exit_shared.rs`).

Note: under load, the quick gate marked `the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level` slow (>60 s with 8 test threads) in the first run, not in the final run. The test plans one 60 x 40 area on two levels.

Heavy step: none. This is a P2 issue, and AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a targeted heavy step only to a P1 PR under the safety floor.

Changelog: The 2D Adaptive takes a start point and an exit point: the entry goes down at the start point and the cleared area grows from there, and the last pass of each level runs back along its closing ride to the point nearest the exit point; a point that the plan cannot hold is refused by name.
